sentences.text:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Shree Chandrashekhar Hon'Ble Mr. Justice
Ratnaker Bhengra
For the Appellant : Mr. A.K. Kashyap, Sr. Advocate Ms. Supriya Dayal,
Advocate For the State : Mrs. Vandana Bharti, App

---------------
Order No. 04/ Dated:22nd March 2023 I.A. No. 1530 of 2023 This interlocutory application has been filed seeking suspension of sentence pending Cr. Appeal (DB) No. 1248 of 2022.
In Sessions Trial No. 289 of 2021, the appellant has been convicted and sentenced to RI for twelve years.
The learned Trial Judge has imposed a fine of Rs.25,000/- upon the convict to be paid to the prosecutrix with a default stipulation to undergo SI for one year.
Sessions Trial No. 289 of 2021 has commenced on the basis of Danda PS Case No. 02 of 2021 which was registered after the prosecutrix gave her written complaint to the police.
In the trial, the prosecution has examined ten witnesses, out of whom PW3 is the prosecutrix.
PW2, PW5, PW6 and PW7 did not support the prosecution and they were declared hostile.
PW1 was tendered for cross-examination and PW9 and PW10 are hearsay witnesses.
The medical evidence which was tendered through PW8 Dr. Mahjabi Yamani is to the effect that no trace of external or internal injury was detected when the prosecutrix was clinically examined by her.
PW8 has rendered an opinion that no evidence of recent sexual activity was found by her over the person of the prosecutrix.

The Trial Court has referred to the application made by the prosecutrix in her written complaint to arrive at the conclusion that the delay in lodging the First Information Report has been explained by Ajit Kumar @ Rahul Kumar Choudhary vs The State Of Jharkhand on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33796815/
1 the prosecution.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned Trial Judge has placed implicit reliance on the evidence of the prosecutrix 2 Cr. Appeal (DB) No. 1248 of 2022 to hold that the appellant is guilty under section 376 of the Indian Penal Code.

Mrs. Vandana Bharti, the learned APP has submitted that the perpetrator of the sexual offence against whom a finding of guilt has been recorded by the learned Additional Sessions Judge is not entitled for suspension of sentence and, moreover, the appellant has remained in custody only for about six months.

Mr. A.K. Kashyap, the learned senior counsel has submitted that the appellant was granted anticipatory bail in ABA No. 3830 of 2021 vide order dated 30th June 2021 and he never misused the privilege of anticipatory bail during the trial.
The learned senior counsel has referred to the examination-in-chief of PW3 whereunder she has stated that she on her own has accompanied the appellant and went to his house.
She has further stated in her cross-examination that the appellant did not sexually ravished her forcibly (             ).
Having regard to the aforesaid facts and circumstances in the case, we are inclined to allow this interlocutory application for suspension of sentence.

Accordingly, Ajit Kumar @ Rahul Kumar Choudhary, the appellant, is directed to be released on bail, during pendency of this appeal, on furnishing bail bond of Rs.10,000/- (rupees ten thousand only) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Additional Sessions Judge-V, Garhwa in Sessions Trial No.
289 of 2021, subject to the conditions that the appellant shall remain physically present or through his authorized counsel in the Court whenever this criminal appeal is listed for hearing in the Court,
however, if no one appears on his behalf on the day when this criminal appeal is listed on Board for hearing the State may file an application for recall of this order.
I.A. No. 1530 of 2023 stands allowed, in the aforesaid terms.
Let a copy of this order be transmitted to the Court concerned and the concerned Jail Superintendent through 'FAX'.

(Shree Chandrashekhar, J.) (Ratnaker Bhengra, J.) S.B./Nibha Ajit Kumar @ Rahul Kumar Choudhary vs The State Of Jharkhand on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33796815/
